cues.text: Hi, Julie, it’s Ricky.
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Hi, Ricky, how are you? I noticed you weren’t in Psychology today.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: I'm feeling sick, so I didn’t go to school today. Would you mind telling me what I missed in class?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Sure thing. I’m sorry you’re not feeling well! Anyway, we spent most of the class talking about a new essay that Professor Johnson assigned. You need to choose one of the bold headings from the note system and research it.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Wow, I picked the wrong day to miss class, huh?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: You sure did.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Could you tell me the specific requirements of this paper?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Sure. You need to find scientific research that supports your claim as one of your references. It can be from some of the case studies we discussed in class, or you can find your own. Or even better, you can conduct your own research! I’m sure that would get you an
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Have you decided what you’re going to do yet? Also, where are you getting your references?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Yeah, I’m going to research facial recognition by infants. I’ve already found a few experiments in scientific journals. That would probably be a good start for you - there are tons of journals in the library.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Great idea, thanks. I’m considering writing my essay on the effects of one of the psychotropic drugs we talked about in class. I’m sure there is lots of stuff about it on the Internet. Are we allowed to use information from the Internet?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Sure, you can use that as long as it’s not your main source for information. You’ll probably want to cite some of the experiments we went over.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Good idea, thanks. I’m gonna try to find some information from a bunch of different sources.
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Are there any specifications on how the essay should be written?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Yeah, Professor Johnson wants it double-spaced. It should be between 6 to 10 pages long.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: 6 to 10 pages? That’s so much! It’s going to take forever.
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: I know. The whole class groaned when he said that. Anyway, you also need to put the title in italics, and...
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Wait, each section heading, or just the main heading?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Only the main heading should be in italics. I think section titles are supposed to be in the same format, but maybe in bold. You’ll have to check that in class next time.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Oh okay. So I take it that the report has to be typed since there are so many requirements. What are the other formatting requirements?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: Yep, it’s got to be typed. Aside from that, there are still a few more specifications. You should number each page. Make sure it goes up in the top right corner.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Okay, I’ll make sure to write that down. I always forget to number the pages. Do we need to title and date each page, too?
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: You need the shortened title on every page, but no need to include the date. That should just be on the cover page.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Okay, thanks.
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: No problem. Also, make sure the margins are 3.25 pixels wide..
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: What? I’m not even sure how to do that.
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: It’s okay, I can show you. It’s really easy. I think that’s all the directions he gave us. A lot of formatting requirements, but we have the freedom to research many things that we like, so that’s good. Oh, I almost forgot - remember to put down your ID number on your report.
cues.speaker: JULIE

cues.text: Thanks so much for your help. I’ll see you in class Monday!
cues.speaker: RICKY

cues.text: No problem, glad I could help. See you later.
cues.speaker: JULIE
